question.text: If one of the diameter of the circle, given by the equation $x^{2}+y^{2}+4 x+6 y-12=0,$ is a chord of a circle $S,$ whose centre is $(2,-3$ ), the radius of $S$ is

solution.text: Given, equation of circle is $x^{2}+y^{2}+4 x+6 y-12=0$ Centre $C(-2,-3)$ and radius $=\sqrt{(-2)^{2}+(-3)^{2}+12}=5$ $$ x^{2}+y^{2}+4 x+6 y-12=0 $$ $$ \begin{aligned} C_{1} C_{2} &=\sqrt{\left(2+{2})^{2}+(-3+3)^{2}\right.} \\ &=\sqrt{(4)^{2}+(0)^{2}}=4 \end{aligned} $$ $\therefore$ Radius of circle, $S$ $$ =\sqrt{(4)^{2}+({5})^{2}}=\sqrt{16+25}=\sqrt{41} \text { unit } $$
